data.name: Cyrus
data.gender_notes: Cyrus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Persian king who freed the Jews from Babylonian captivity in 538 BC. He allowed the Israelites to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the Temple. The name Cyrus carries the meaning “Persian king, ruler” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Cyrus usually hope their child will grow to embody persian king, ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A leader who brings freedom and restoration.
data.etymology: Cyrus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Persian king, ruler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cyrus total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: כורש
in_hebrew.long_meaning: כורש היה מלך פרסי שחרר את היהודים מגלות בבל, והתיר להם לבנות מחדש את בית המקדש בירושלים, כפי שמוזכר בספר עזרא ודברי הימים

in_greek.name: Κύρος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Κύρος ήταν βασιλιάς της Περσίας που απελευθέρωσε τους Εβραίους από την εξορία στη Βαβυλώνα, και τους επέτρεψε να ξαναχτίσουν τον Ναό της Ιερουσαλήμ, όπως αναφέρεται στο βιβλίο του Εσδρα και των Παραλειπομένων

in_latin.name: Cyrus
in_latin.long_meaning: Cyrus fuit rex Persarum qui Iudaeos a captivitate Babylonica liberavit, et eis permisit ut templum Hierosolymitanum restituerent, ut in libro Esdrae et Paralipomenon memoratur

in_english.name: Cyrus
in_english.long_meaning: Cyrus was a great king of Persia who liberated the Jews from Babylonian captivity, and allowed them to rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem, as mentioned in the book of Ezra and Chronicles, symbolizing freedom and redemption

data.cultural_impact: Cyrus's willingness to allow the Jewish exiles to return to their homeland and rebuild their temple marked a significant moment in history. It set a precedent for later emperors and rulers to tolerate religious freedom, contributing to the spread of Christianity and other religions.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian Bible, Cyrus is mentioned as God's anointed one in Isaiah 45:1, predicting his role in freeing the Jews and allowing them to rebuild their temple. This prophecy supports the belief among Christians that God is actively involved in human history and uses worldly leaders to fulfill His will.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cyrus is a name of Persian origin, meaning "anointed one" or "god's messenger," reflecting the biblical king Cyrus who freed the Jews from captivity and facilitated the return to Jerusalem to rebuild the Temple. In Christianity, it symbolizes divine intervention and the call to serve as a messenger or leader in God's plan.

biblical_reference.note: Cyrus is mentioned as the king who issued a decree allowing the Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the Temple

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that In the Bible, Cyrus is the king who allows the Jews to return to Jerusalem. The name Cyrus carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Cyrus remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Peter Cyrus from Athens, Greece embodies the meaning of Cyrus - "Persian king, ruler". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
